names_for.catalogue_side: Off-the-Shelf Datasets (also 'licensed datasets'; Datatang in Chinese: 版权数据集, 'copyright datasets')
names_for.custom_side: Data Service / 'Bespoke data collection services' / 'customized data collection' (Datatang: 数据定制)

operator_role.note: Nexdata Technology Inc. is licensor of record on the only published licence (the research template), and listings sell data Nexdata says it owns or holds rights to. The commercial licence text is not public.

economics_model.note: Nexdata sells its own or licensed-in inventory at its own prices; no third-party seller programme or commission was found.

who_pays_fee.note: No marketplace fee: Nexdata sells its own inventory as principal. Whatever Datarade charges Nexdata for its storefront is not published.

supply_models.note: Own collection: data factory, collectors wearing Pico headsets, recruited phone owners, and Datatang's crowd platform [c105]. Licensed in: creator/photographer photo and video and TV footage 'obtained through authorized channels'; the channel and licensor are never named. No provider or contributor-upload programme was found, and no evidence that client-commissioned data is relisted.

custody_model.note: The research licence assumes the licensee holds copies on its own storage and must destroy them. Datarade lists S3, SFTP, email and API delivery, but that list looks like a generic form.

transaction_mode.note: Every listing ends in 'Ask for a Quote' or 'Request Information'; no checkout was found. Research datasets are released by application form.

public_prices.note: nexdata.ai shows no prices. Its Datarade storefront (data.nexdata.ai) shows 'Starts at' one-off floor prices (USD 10K, 20K or 100K) on 158 of 159 products (the profiler's own count of every storefront product page on 2026-10-01; one says 'Pricing available upon request').

licence_model.note: Two tracks: a standard free research licence (published template: non-commercial, one year) and a commercial licence tailored by application, geography and usage scenario, which is negotiated and not published.

exclusivity_offered.note: The research template is non-exclusive; no page says whether commercial buyers can get exclusivity.

public_listing.note: Anonymous visitors see full listing pages with specs and sample images; the site's sitemap.xml lists about 445 dataset pages (the profiler's own count on 2026-10-01).

buyer_vetting.note: No account needed to browse. Buyers submit a form asking for a company email and project details; purchases are accepted at Nexdata's discretion; free research data goes only to non-commercial organisations.

sample_mechanics.note: Listings also embed a few sample images in the browser; fuller samples are requested via the 'Get Data Samples' form.

versioning.note: No listing, licence or storefront page mentions versions, updates or withdrawals.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Only marketing assertions (GDPR/CCPA/PIPL compliance, 'collected with consent'). No consent or release evidence is offered to buyers, and the research template has no consent warranty [c059]. The commercial licence may say more, but it is not public.

contributor_pay_model.note: No page found says how collectors, crowd workers or the creators of licensed-in photos and videos are paid.

erasure_after_sale.note: Evidence covers only the research licence (destroy all copies within 5 days of expiry and certify). Commercial terms are unknown, and data-subject erasure after sale is not addressed anywhere.

quality_evidence.note: Nexdata is both operator and data owner, so 'operator verified' here means Nexdata's own QA claims (three-round inspection, ISO 9001). The only external check cited is iBeta Level 2 for anti-spoofing data.

Q1.answer: Nexdata says it has served 1,000+ companies and gives free speech datasets to universities. Its one worked example is a client that bought part of the 100,000-hour ego-centric dataset to start fast, then commissioned custom collection. Datarade floor prices run from USD 10K to 100K per one-off purchase.

Q2.answer: Nexdata sells through its own site (quote only) and through a Datarade-powered storefront that shows floor prices and a 'Request Information' button, and it recruits resale partners. It never says what the third-party channel gives it.

Q3.answer: Inventory comes from Nexdata's own collection (a data factory, headset-wearing collectors, recruited phone owners, a Datatang crowd platform) and from licensed-in creator, photographer and TV content 'obtained through authorized channels'. The rights are asserted, never documented, and there is no third-party provider programme.

Q4.answer: Custom-service pages promise an NDA and 'data destroyed upon delivery', which suggests commissioned data is not relisted. No carve-out terms and no after-the-fact term change were found.

Q5.answer: Nexdata Technology Inc. (California) is licensor of record on the research template. That template gives no warranty from Nexdata and puts third-party liability on the licensee; the website terms disclaim everything 'as is'. The commercial licence's warranties and indemnities are not public.

Q6.answer: The data is copied to the buyer: the research licensee stores copies and must destroy them, and the catalogue promises delivery 'in seconds'. Delivery channels for commercial sales are not documented beyond Datarade's generic list.

Q7.answer: Listings and service pages assert GDPR/CCPA/PIPL compliance and 'consent with proper authorization'. Face-data listings are silent on consent, and creator works are described only as 'released by the author'. No consent or release documents are published, and the privacy policy does not cover data subjects.

Q8.answer: The research licence is non-exclusive, non-transferable and non-commercial, forbids derivatives (models included), runs one year, and requires confidentiality, per-quantity leakage damages and certified destruction. Commercial terms are 'tailored' and unpublished. Nexdata cites URL encryption and anti-hotlinking but no fingerprinting.

Q9.answer: Deals close through sales: 'Ask for a Quote' forms, purchases subject to Nexdata's acceptance, and licence terms discussed before purchase. Nexdata sells as principal; Datarade shows 'starts at' prices but still routes buyers to a request form.

Q10.answer: A listing is one dataset with a specification table and samples, and part of a dataset can be bought. Research licences expire after one year with mandatory deletion. Nothing is published on versions, updates or withdrawals.

Q11.answer: Listings show a spec table, stated label accuracy and embedded sample images; fuller samples come on request. Nexdata cites three-round QA with sampling rates, ISO 9001/27001/27701, and iBeta certification for anti-spoofing data.

Q12.answer: 'Off-the-Shelf Datasets' and 'Data Service' (also 'Bespoke data collection services') sit side by side in the navigation. Nexdata pitches the catalogue as the fast start and custom collection as the gap-filler.

sections.positioning: Nexdata (NEXDATA TECHNOLOGY INC, California office [c102]; 'based in Singapore' per its About page [c016]) sells an off-the-shelf catalogue alongside collection and annotation services [c007]. It is technically linked to Datatang, the Beijing AI-data company with stock code 831428 [c087]: Nexdata pages embed a datatang.com hostname [c089]. No page states the corporate relationship. Nexdata says it was founded in 2011 and Datatang says 2010 [c007][c087].
sections.supply: Supply is mainly Nexdata's own production: a Physical AI data factory it says is 10,000+ m² [c003], collectors wearing Pico headsets [c094], phone owners recruited for projects [c097], 20,000+ annotators [c010] and Datatang's crowd platform Shujiajia [c105]. Large photo and video sets are licensed in from creators, photographers and TV sources 'through authorized channels' [c018][c083][c084][c085], but the channel is never named. A Linkerbot alliance co-creates dexterous-hand data [c099]. The partner programme recruits sellers, not data suppliers [c071].
sections.object_model: The unit is a dataset listing with a specification table (size, demographics, device, format, accuracy) [c030][c032]. Buyers can buy part of a dataset [c091]. The research template lists datasets by ID with a market value in USD [c051]. No versioning or revision model is published.
sections.listing: Listings are public, with specs, a few sample images and the line 'This is a paid dataset licensed for commercial use' [c025]. The buttons are 'Get Data Samples' and 'Ask for a Quote' [c027][c026]. Face listings give nationality and demographic counts but say nothing about consent [c031][c033]. Headline sizes: 30 million videos [c019], 1,000+ to 1,500+ datasets [c009][c095].
sections.discovery: Category pages filter by task type and modality [c036] and offer a downloadable catalogue request and 'Contact Sales' [c037]. A second storefront on Datarade (data.nexdata.ai) lists 159 products [c077].
sections.trust: Trust rests on Nexdata's assertions: GDPR/CCPA compliance [c015], per-listing GDPR/CCPA/PIPL statements [c035], 'consent with proper authorization' [c075], ISO 27001/27701 [c068], and iBeta certification for anti-spoofing data [c086]. No consent documents are shown. The website terms give everything 'as is' [c042], and the research template gives no warranty from Nexdata [c059].
sections.transaction: Every purchase is sales-led. A form asks for a company email and a data-requirement description [c028][c029]. Purchases are subject to Nexdata's acceptance [c039], and licensing is discussed before purchase [c012]. Datarade pages also end in 'Request Information' [c081]. Research datasets are released after a form and review [c063].
sections.pricing: nexdata.ai publishes no prices. On its Datarade storefront, products carry one-off 'Starts at' prices: USD 20K for most, including the video datasets [c078]; USD 10K for face and anti-spoofing sets [c080]; USD 100K for 100,000 hours of ego-centric data [c079]. Monthly, yearly and usage-based licences are marked not available.
sections.licence: Two tracks. Research: a published template that is free, non-exclusive, non-transferable and non-commercial, with no derivatives (models included) [c048][c049], one year [c054], confidentiality [c058], attribution with notice [c056] and a speech-set cap of 4 per applicant [c062]. Converting to commercial use means paying full market value [c052]. Commercial: 'tailored' by application, geography and usage scenario [c011]; its text is not public. The website terms bar resellers [c040].
sections.custody: The data is copied to the buyer. The research licensee holds copies and must destroy them [c055]; the catalogue promises delivery 'in seconds' [c103]; Datarade lists S3, SFTP and API delivery [c104]. Nexdata protects its own hosting with URL encryption, anti-hotlinking and anti-crawling [c069].
sections.vetting: Quality control is internal: self-inspection, then initial inspection sampling at least 50%, then final inspection sampling 30%, under ISO 9001 [c065][c066][c067]. Listings state label accuracy, for example above 97% [c032] and above 95% [c034]. No independent audit is cited apart from iBeta [c086].
sections.contributor_pay: Not published. Case studies describe recruiting UK iPhone owners [c097] and headset-wearing collectors [c094], and Datatang runs a crowd-task platform [c105], but no page says how any of them, or the creators of licensed-in works [c021], are paid.
sections.post_sale: Research licensees must destroy all copies within 5 days of expiry and certify it [c055]. Leakage triggers full market value plus per-quantity damages [c053]. The website terms incorporate return and shipping policies that are not linked [c043]. Nothing covers data-subject erasure after sale.
sections.catalogue_custom: The navigation splits 'Off-the-Shelf Datasets' from 'Data Service' [c017], and press uses 'Bespoke data collection services' [c006]. Nexdata frames the catalogue as the fast start and custom collection as the gap-filler [c092][c091]. Custom work comes with an NDA and 'data destroyed upon delivery' [c074][c076]. Stated capacity: 50,000+ hours/month of bespoke UMI data [c004].
sections.changes: Active: news dated 17 Sep 2026 announces an AI-data-infrastructure award [c002][c001]. The facility claim grew from 8,000+ m² (Jul 2026) [c096] to 10,000+ m² (Sep 2026) [c003]. The strategic direction is Physical AI, including a Linkerbot alliance [c099]. The website terms date from May 2022 [c038].
sections.demand: Nexdata claims 1,000+ customer companies [c008]. Its one described buyer pattern is to buy part of the catalogue to start, then commission custom collection [c091]. Universities receive free speech data and are listed as logos [c061][c057]. There is a partner programme to extend sales abroad [c071]. None of this is independently verified.
sections.regulation: Nexdata's privacy policy covers site visitors and customers only [c100], and it shares customer data within its corporate group [c101]. The research template sends disputes to a Chinese 'people's court' [c060]; the website terms impose arbitration [c041].

buyer_journey.step: Lands on nexdata.ai: 'Off-the-Shelf Datasets' and 'Data Service' menus side by side, with a claim of 1,000+ ready datasets 'delivered in seconds'.
Browses a category page (for example Computer Vision), filters by task type and modality; no prices are shown; 'Get Datasets Catalog' and 'Contact Sales' buttons.

Opens a listing: spec table, stated label accuracy, a few embedded sample images and 'This is a paid dataset licensed for commercial use'. For licensed-in video, rights are described only as copyright-cleared works 'released by the author'.
Clicks 'Get Data Samples' or 'Ask for a Quote' and fills a form: name, phone, company, company email, and a requirement of at least 5 words.
Alternatively finds the same products on Nexdata's Datarade storefront with 'Starts at' one-off prices (USD 10K to 100K), but still presses 'Request Information'.
Negotiates with sales: licence tailored to application, geography and usage scenario. The purchase is subject to Nexdata's acceptance; resellers are refused.
Receives a copy of the data (the delivery mechanism for commercial sales is not documented) under an unpublished commercial licence with Nexdata Technology Inc.

Academic route instead: applies through the sponsored-datasets form (at most 4 speech sets), signs the free one-year research licence, and must credit Nexdata, keep the data confidential and destroy it at expiry.

conflicts.resolution: The facility size rose from 8,000+ m² (8 Jul 2026) to 10,000+ m² (17 Sep 2026). The newer figure is used; the pages do not say whether this is growth or a different measure.

Speech inventory is 200,000 hours on the partner page (undated) but 'over 10 million hours' in the July 2026 article. Datarade copy says 3 million hours. The figures cannot be reconciled from the sources.

The homepage says 'over 1000' off-the-shelf datasets and the July 2026 article says '1,500+ licensed datasets'; the site's sitemap.xml lists about 445 dataset pages (the profiler's own count). The claimed counts are vendor-stated and not reconciled.
Nexdata says it was founded in 2011; Datatang says 2010. These may be different entities' founding dates; the relationship is not published.

leads.why: Datatang (831428) periodic reports should give revenue split between datasets and custom services, and name Nexdata-related subsidiaries; the disclosure search was not reachable without web search.
Linked from Datatang's footer: a Chinese dataset platform with token-based ('Token计费') pricing, run by 北京帕依提提科技有限公司. Its relationship to Datatang is unstated.
Datatang's crowdsourcing app; JS-only. The task and pay pages could answer contributor_pay_model.
Customer service portal, JS-only; it might show how delivery and entitlements work after purchase.
Datarade's own provider profile and terms could show what the storefront costs Nexdata and whether it earns referral fees.
Open autonomous-driving dataset linked from both Nexdata's and Datatang's footers; shows the shared web estate.
